plot: The morning after the bare tree Max wants to send his first letter to cousin Luna before the noon mail, but his painted M looks like a blue pancake and Dog walks blue paw prints onto Grandma's sofa; Mouse asks whether little Luna can even read, so Max paints pictures of their week instead, despairs that it is a messy scribble, until Bird sees he painted on an upside-down paper and turning it round shows Nutty, the snow and his budding tree; Max signs with a paw print, the letter goes just in time, and three days later a pink envelope with a tiny white paw print arrives.

script.title: Max Can't Write! His First Letter to Luna

beats.say: Oh no! My paw slipped! Now it's a big blue blob!
Max! You painted the paper, the rug and your own nose!
How do cats write letters? I can't even make an M!
It's a quiet morning, the day after the bare tree.
Max wants to send his first letter. To his cousin Luna.
I miss her. I want to tell her about the tiny buds.
Mouse knows her letters. Maybe she can help you.
Of course! Lesson one. The letter M. For Max!
Up, down, up, down. Like two mountains.
Mountains. Easy. I climb things all the time.
Max dips his paw in the blue paint and tries.
Up... down... up... SPLAT!
Hmm. That M looks like a blue pancake.
It's not a pancake. It's a very modern M.
Let's try the A. A is like a little tent.
A tent... with a blob on top. Hmm. A blue blob tent.
Can I help? I'm good at paws! I have four!
Dog steps in the paint. Then he walks across the paper.
Then across the rug. Then up onto the sofa.
Dog! My sofa! It's covered in blue paw prints!
Now the sofa can send a letter too!
This is a disaster. Luna will never get my letter.
The mail lady comes at noon, Max. Only one hour left.
One hour? I can't learn the whole alphabet in one hour!
Wait, Max. How old is Luna?
She's little. Littler than me. Why?
Can Luna read letters?
Um... no. Grandma reads her stories at bedtime.
Then she won't read words anyway! But she can read pictures!
Pictures? Like drawing? I can draw!
Draw her everything you want to tell her. One picture for each.
Max gets a fresh paper. He thinks very hard.
Um, Max? Your paper is upside...
Shh! An artist needs quiet.
Swish. Swoosh. Dab, dab, dab. Max paints and paints.
Here is Nutty, eating seeds from my fur.
Here is the snow. And Bird, and the feeder.
And here is my tree, with a hundred tiny buds.
Then Max steps back to look at his picture.
Oh no. It's all wrong. It's just a big messy scribble.
It looks like... a blue spaghetti dinner?
Luna will think I can't do anything right.
Ten minutes until the mail lady comes, Max.
Hello, everyone! Why is the sofa blue?
Long story, Bird. Very blue story.
It's a mess. But it's all I have. Let's send it anyway.
That's brave, Max. Let me fold it for the envelope.
Grandma picks up the picture. She turns it around to fold it.
And then Grandma stops. She looks. She smiles.
Max... come and look at this. The right way up.
I tried to tell you! The paper was upside down!
Max walks over. Slowly. And he looks.
And now, everyone can see it.
Oh, Max. There's Nutty. There's the snow. There's your tree!
And there's me! I'm the blue spaghetti!
It's not a scribble. It's our whole week!
And there's me, eating at the feeder! You got my feathers!
I drew it upside down, and it still came out right!
You don't need fancy words to tell a friend you miss her.
Wait. One more thing. A letter needs my name.
Max dips his paw in the paint. And presses it down.
There. A paw print. That's how cats sign their name.
Grandma folds the picture into an envelope.
Just in time. Here comes the mail lady!
The letter goes into the mail bag. Off to Luna!
A picture letter! Luna is going to love it!
Can I send the sofa next?
Grandma looks at Dog. Dog looks at the sofa.
First, you can help me clean it, Dog.
Friends don't need perfect words. They need a little piece of you.
Three days later, there's a plop at the front door.
A letter! For me? From who?
On the pink envelope, there's one tiny white paw print.
Grandma! I think Luna wrote back!
What did Luna send to Max?
